content.title: About
content.content: Triscuit crackers are crunchy wheat crackers made from whole grain wheat, baked without added sugar or artificial flavors. They have a light, slightly nutty taste and a distinctive woven texture created by pressing the dough into a grid.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Triscuit was first introduced in the United States in 1901 as "wheat biscuits".
The traditional manufacturing process presses the dough into a woven pattern, giving the crackers their signature look.
They are commonly used as a base for cheese, pâté, or vegetable toppings.
The original recipe contains only whole wheat, vegetable oil, and salt.
Their texture allows them to stay crisp even after a brief dip in sauces.

items.title: Source of whole grains
items.content: Whole wheat provides fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals that support healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The absence of added sugars makes them suitable for low‑carb or reduced‑sugar diets.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: A modest amount of vegetable oil supplies essential unsaturated fats.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The crunchy texture and fiber help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Reduced sodium option
items.content: A no‑salt version is available for those monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Wheat/gluten allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or gluten intolerance should avoid these crackers.

items.title: High sodium (regular version)
items.content: Salt is used for flavor; choose the low‑salt version if you need to limit sodium.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While light, they are more calorie‑dense than fresh vegetables, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Triscuit crackers are great as a standalone snack, paired with cheese, hummus, avocado, or as a base for canapés. Lightly warming them in the oven can enhance their crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed package. Once opened, consume within 2–3 weeks to maintain crispness and flavor.
